prompt:
A hat contains six slips of paper numbered from $1$ to $6$. Amelie and Bob each choose three slips from the hat without replacing any of the slips. Each of them adds up the numbers on his or her slips.

Determine the largest possible difference between Amelie's total and Bob's total. Explain how you found this difference.

solutions.title: Big three vs small three
solutions.body:
The difference is largest when one person has the three largest numbers and the other the three smallest: $4 + 5 + 6 = 15$ and $1 + 2 + 3 = 6$. Difference $9$.

**Answer: 9**

solutions.title: Using the total
solutions.body:
The totals add to $21$, so if one total is $T$ the difference is $|2T - 21|$. The largest possible $T$ is $15$ and the smallest $6$; either gives $|30 - 21| = |12 - 21| = 9$.

**Answer: 9**

prompt:
A hat contains six slips of paper numbered from $1$ to $6$. Amelie and Bob each choose three slips from the hat without replacing any of the slips. Each of them adds up the numbers on his or her slips.

List all possible groups of three slips that Amelie can choose so that her total is one more than Bob's total.

solutions.title: Her total must be 11
solutions.body:
The six numbers add to $21$, so Amelie's total $A$ and Bob's $B$ satisfy $A + B = 21$ and $A = B + 1$, giving $A = 11$.

Triples from $1$–$6$ with sum $11$: $\{1, 4, 6\}$, $\{2, 3, 6\}$, $\{2, 4, 5\}$. (With $6$: the other two sum to $5$: $1 + 4$, $2 + 3$. Without $6$ but with $5$: the other two sum to $6$ from $1$–$4$: $2 + 4$. Without $5$ or $6$: at most $2 + 3 + 4 = 9$.)

**Answer: $\{1,4,6\}$, $\{2,3,6\}$, $\{2,4,5\}$**

solutions.title: Check with Bob's slips
solutions.body: Bob gets the other three slips, which must total $10$. The complements of Amelie's groups are $\{2, 3, 5\}$, $\{1, 4, 5\}$ and $\{1, 3, 6\}$, each summing to $10$ ✓. Listing all triples with sum $10$ gives exactly these three, confirming the list.

prompt:
A hat contains six slips of paper numbered from $1$ to $6$. Amelie and Bob each choose three slips from the hat without replacing any of the slips. Each of them adds up the numbers on his or her slips.

Explain why it is impossible for Amelie and Bob to have the same total no matter which three slips each chooses.
answer: Their totals add to $1 + \cdots + 6 = 21$, which is odd, so they can't be equal.

solutions.title: Odd total
solutions.body: Every slip is taken, so the two totals add to $21$. Equal totals would add to an even number. $21$ is odd, so the totals are never equal. ∎

solutions.title: Half of 21
solutions.body: Equal totals would each be $21 \div 2 = 10.5$, not an integer. ∎

prompt:
A hat contains six slips of paper numbered from $1$ to $6$. Amelie and Bob each choose three slips from the hat without replacing any of the slips. Each of them adds up the numbers on his or her slips.

If more slips of paper are added to the hat, numbered consecutively from $7$ to $n$, what is the smallest value of $n > 6$ so that Amelie and Bob can each choose half of the slips numbered from $1$ to $n$ and obtain the same total? Explain why this value of $n$ works.

solutions.title: n must be even; try 8
solutions.body:
Each takes half the slips, so $n$ is even; $n = 7$ is impossible, so $n \ge 8$. For $n = 8$ the total is $36$, so each needs $18$: Amelie takes $1, 2, 7, 8$ and Bob takes $3, 4, 5, 6$. Both total $18$.

**Answer: $n = 8$**

solutions.title: Pairing trick
solutions.body:
For $n = 8$, pair the numbers as $(1, 8), (2, 7), (3, 6), (4, 5)$, each summing to $9$. Giving two pairs to each person gives equal totals $18$. And $n = 7$ fails because $7$ slips can't be split in half.

**Answer: $n = 8$**

prompt:
In the diagram, $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DE$, $EF$, $FG$, $GH$, and $HK$ all have length $4$, and all angles are right angles, with the exception of the angles at $D$ and $F$. (The figure is a rectangle $ABHK$ with $C$ and $G$ on $BH$; $CD$ and $GF$ rise vertically from $BH$, and $E$ lies between them below $DF$, with $\angle DEF = 90^\circ$.)

Determine the length of $DF$.

solutions.title: Pythagoras
solutions.body:
$\triangle DEF$ has a right angle at $E$ and legs $4, 4$: $DF^2 = 16 + 16 = 32$, $DF = 4\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $4\sqrt2$**

solutions.title: 45-45-90 triangle
solutions.body:
An isosceles right triangle's hypotenuse is $\sqrt2$ times a leg: $DF = 4\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $4\sqrt2$**

prompt:
In the diagram, $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DE$, $EF$, $FG$, $GH$, and $HK$ all have length $4$, and all angles are right angles, with the exception of the angles at $D$ and $F$. (The figure is a rectangle $ABHK$ with $C$ and $G$ on $BH$; $CD$ and $GF$ rise vertically from $BH$, and $E$ lies between them below $DF$, with $\angle DEF = 90^\circ$.)

If perpendicular $EM$ is drawn from $E$ to $DF$, what is the length of $EM$? Explain how you got your answer.

solutions.title: Area two ways
solutions.body:
Area of $\triangle DEF = \frac12 \cdot 4 \cdot 4 = 8$. Also area $= \frac12 \cdot DF \cdot EM = \frac12 \cdot 4\sqrt2 \cdot EM$. So $EM = \frac{16}{4\sqrt2} = 2\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt2$**

solutions.title: Half the hypotenuse
solutions.body:
$M$ is the midpoint of $DF$ (the triangle is isosceles), so $DM = 2\sqrt2$, and $\triangle DME$ is a $45$-$45$-$90$ triangle, giving $EM = DM = 2\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt2$**

prompt:
In the diagram, $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DE$, $EF$, $FG$, $GH$, and $HK$ all have length $4$, and all angles are right angles, with the exception of the angles at $D$ and $F$. (The figure is a rectangle $ABHK$ with $C$ and $G$ on $BH$; $CD$ and $GF$ rise vertically from $BH$, and $E$ lies between them below $DF$, with $\angle DEF = 90^\circ$.)

If perpendicular $EP$ is drawn from $E$ to $AK$, what is the length of $EP$? Explain how you got your answer.

solutions.title: Stack the distances
solutions.body:
$D$ and $F$ are both $4$ above line $BH$ (since $CD = GF = 4$), and $DF$ is horizontal; $AK$ is $4$ below $BH$. $E$ is $EM = 2\sqrt2$ below $DF$, so it is $4 - 2\sqrt2$ above $BH$, and
$$EP = 4 + (4 - 2\sqrt2) = 8 - 2\sqrt2.$$

**Answer: $8 - 2\sqrt2$** (about $5.17$)

solutions.title: Coordinates
solutions.body:
Put $A = (0, 0)$, so $B = (0, 4)$, $C = (4, 4)$, $D = (4, 8)$, and $F = (4 + 4\sqrt2, 8)$. $E$ is below the midpoint of $DF$ at depth $2\sqrt2$: $E = (4 + 2\sqrt2,\ 8 - 2\sqrt2)$. $AK$ is the $x$-axis, so $EP = 8 - 2\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $8 - 2\sqrt2$**

prompt:
In the diagram, $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DE$, $EF$, $FG$, $GH$, and $HK$ all have length $4$, and all angles are right angles, with the exception of the angles at $D$ and $F$. (The figure is a rectangle $ABHK$ with $C$ and $G$ on $BH$; $CD$ and $GF$ rise vertically from $BH$, and $E$ lies between them below $DF$, with $\angle DEF = 90^\circ$.)

What is the area of figure $ABCDEFGHK$? Explain how you got your answer.

solutions.title: Two rectangles minus a triangle
solutions.body:
Join $DF$ and $CG$. The figure is rectangle $ABHK$ plus rectangle $CGFD$ minus $\triangle DEF$.

- $CG = DF = 4\sqrt2$, so $BH = 4 + 4\sqrt2 + 4 = 8 + 4\sqrt2$; area of $ABHK = 4(8 + 4\sqrt2) = 32 + 16\sqrt2$.
- $CGFD$: $4 \times 4\sqrt2 = 16\sqrt2$.
- $\triangle DEF$: $8$.

Area $= 32 + 16\sqrt2 + 16\sqrt2 - 8 = 24 + 32\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $24 + 32\sqrt2$** (about $69.25$)

solutions.title: Shoelace with coordinates
solutions.body:
With $A(0,0)$, $B(0,4)$, $C(4,4)$, $D(4,8)$, $E(4+2\sqrt2, 8-2\sqrt2)$, $F(4+4\sqrt2, 8)$, $G(4+4\sqrt2, 4)$, $H(8+4\sqrt2, 4)$, $K(8+4\sqrt2, 0)$: the region below $y = 4$ is $4(8 + 4\sqrt2)$, and above it is the $4\sqrt2 \times 4$ rectangle with the triangle $DEF$ (area $8$) removed. Total $32 + 16\sqrt2 + 16\sqrt2 - 8 = 24 + 32\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $24 + 32\sqrt2$**

prompt:
In the diagram, a line is drawn through the points $A(0, 16)$ and $B(8, 0)$. Point $P$ is chosen in the first quadrant on the line through $A$ and $B$. Points $C$ and $D$ are then chosen on the $x$-axis and $y$-axis, respectively, so that $PDOC$ is a rectangle.

Determine the equation of the line through $A$ and $B$.

solutions.title: Slope and intercept
solutions.body:
Slope $= \frac{16 - 0}{0 - 8} = -2$, and the $y$-intercept is $16$ (point $A$). So $y = -2x + 16$.

**Answer: $y = -2x + 16$**

solutions.title: Intercept form
solutions.body:
A line with $x$-intercept $8$ and $y$-intercept $16$ is $\frac{x}{8} + \frac{y}{16} = 1$, i.e. $2x + y = 16$.

**Answer: $y = -2x + 16$**

prompt:
In the diagram, a line is drawn through the points $A(0, 16)$ and $B(8, 0)$. Point $P$ is chosen in the first quadrant on the line through $A$ and $B$. Points $C$ and $D$ are then chosen on the $x$-axis and $y$-axis, respectively, so that $PDOC$ is a rectangle.

Determine the coordinates of the point $P$ so that $PDOC$ is a square.

solutions.title: Equal sides
solutions.body:
Let $P = (c, -2c + 16)$. Then $PD = c$ (distance to the $y$-axis) and $PC = -2c + 16$ (distance to the $x$-axis). A square needs $c = -2c + 16$, so $c = \frac{16}{3}$ and $P = \left(\frac{16}3, \frac{16}3\right)$.

**Answer: $\left(\frac{16}{3}, \frac{16}{3}\right)$**

solutions.title: Intersect with y = x
solutions.body:
For a square, $P$ lies on $y = x$. Solving $x = -2x + 16$ gives $x = \frac{16}{3}$.

**Answer: $\left(\frac{16}{3}, \frac{16}{3}\right)$**

prompt:
In the diagram, a line is drawn through the points $A(0, 16)$ and $B(8, 0)$. Point $P$ is chosen in the first quadrant on the line through $A$ and $B$. Points $C$ and $D$ are then chosen on the $x$-axis and $y$-axis, respectively, so that $PDOC$ is a rectangle.

Determine the coordinates of all points $P$ that can be chosen so that the area of rectangle $PDOC$ is $30$.

solutions.title: Area equation
solutions.body:
With $P = (c, -2c + 16)$, the area is $c(-2c + 16) = 30$, i.e. $2c^2 - 16c + 30 = 0$, $c^2 - 8c + 15 = 0$, $(c - 3)(c - 5) = 0$. So $P = (3, 10)$ or $(5, 6)$; both are in the first quadrant and give area $30$.

**Answer: $(3, 10)$ and $(5, 6)$**

solutions.title: Hyperbola meets line
solutions.body:
Area $30$ means $xy = 30$. With $y = 16 - 2x$: $x(16 - 2x) = 30$, the same quadratic, $x = 3$ or $5$. Check: $3 \cdot 10 = 30$ ✓, $5 \cdot 6 = 30$ ✓.

**Answer: $(3, 10)$ and $(5, 6)$**

prompt: When the number $14$ has its digits reversed to form the number $41$, it is increased by $27$. Determine all $2$-digit numbers which are increased by $27$ when their digits are reversed.

solutions.title: Algebra
solutions.body:
For $\underline{a}\,\underline{b} = 10a + b$, reversing gives $10b + a$, an increase of $9(b - a)$. We need $9(b - a) = 27$, so $b = a + 3$ with $a \ge 1$, $b \le 9$: $14, 25, 36, 47, 58, 69$.

**Answer: 14, 25, 36, 47, 58, 69**

solutions.title: Check
solutions.body: $41 - 14 = 52 - 25 = 63 - 36 = 74 - 47 = 85 - 58 = 96 - 69 = 27$ ✓. Any other pair of digits differs by something other than $3$, giving a change other than $27$.

prompt:
Choose any three-digit integer $\underline{a}\,\underline{b}\,\underline{c}$ whose digits are all different. (When an integer is written in terms of its digits as $\underline{a}\,\underline{b}\,\underline{c}$, it means the integer is $100a + 10b + c$.)

Reverse the order of the digits to get a new three-digit integer $\underline{c}\,\underline{b}\,\underline{a}$. Subtract the smaller of these integers from the larger to obtain a three-digit integer $\underline{r}\,\underline{s}\,\underline{t}$, where $r$ is allowed to be $0$. Reverse the order of the digits of this integer to get the integer $\underline{t}\,\underline{s}\,\underline{r}$. Prove that, no matter what three-digit integer $\underline{a}\,\underline{b}\,\underline{c}$ you start with, $\underline{r}\,\underline{s}\,\underline{t} + \underline{t}\,\underline{s}\,\underline{r} = 1089$.
answer: The difference is $99k$ with $k = |a - c| \in \{1, \dots, 9\}$, whose digits are $k - 1,\ 9,\ 10 - k$; reversing and adding gives $100 \cdot 9 + 10 \cdot 18 + 9 = 1089$.

solutions.title: The difference is 99k
solutions.body:
Assume $a > c$ (otherwise swap roles). Then
$$\underline{r}\,\underline{s}\,\underline{t} = (100a + 10b + c) - (100c + 10b + a) = 99(a - c) = 99k,$$
with $k = a - c \in \{1, \dots, 9\}$. Since $99k = 100(k - 1) + 90 + (10 - k)$, its digits are $r = k - 1$, $s = 9$, $t = 10 - k$ (all between $0$ and $9$). Then
$$\underline{r}\,\underline{s}\,\underline{t} + \underline{t}\,\underline{s}\,\underline{r} = 100(r + t) + 20s + (t + r) = 100 \cdot 9 + 180 + 9 = 1089.$$
∎

solutions.title: Check all nine cases
solutions.body: The possible differences are $099, 198, 297, 396, 495, 594, 693, 792, 891$, and their reverses are $990, 891, 792, 693, 594, 495, 396, 297, 198$. Each pair adds to $1089$. ∎

prompt: Suppose that $N = \underline{a}\,\underline{b}\,\underline{c}\,\underline{d}$ is a four-digit integer with $a \le b \le c \le d$. When the order of the digits of $N$ is reversed to form the integer $M$, $N$ is increased by $P$. (Again, the first digit of $P$ is allowed to be $0$.) When the order of the digits of $P$ is reversed, an integer $Q$ is formed. Determine, with justification, all possible values of $P + Q$.
